[notebooks](https://github.com/roboflow/notebooks) | [inference](https://github.com/roboflow/inference) | [autodistill](https://github.com/autodistill/autodistill) | [maestro](https://github.com/roboflow/multimodal-maestro)
📑 Table of Contents - [👋 Hello](#-hello) - [💻 Install](#-install) - [🔥 Quickstart](#-quickstart) - [Models](#models) - [Annotators](#annotators) - [Datasets](#datasets) - [🎬 Tutorials](#-tutorials) - [💜 Built with Supervision](#-built-with-supervision) - [📚 Documentation](#-documentation) - [🏆 Contribution](#-contribution)
## 👋 Hello **We are your essential toolkit for computer vision.** From data loading to real-time zone counting, we provide the building blocks so you can focus on building applications around your models. 🤝 ## 💻 Install Pip install the supervision package in a [**Python>=3.10**](https://www.python.org/) environment. ```bash pip install supervision ``` Read more about conda, mamba, and installing from source in our [guide](https://supervision.roboflow.com/). ## 🔥 Quickstart ### Models Supervision was designed to be model agnostic. Just plug in any classification, detection, or segmentation model. For your convenience, we have created [connectors](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/detection/core/#detections) for the most popular libraries like Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, or Inference. Other integrations, like `rfdetr`, already return `sv.Detections` directly. Install the optional dependencies for this example with `pip install pillow rfdetr`. ```python import supervision as sv from PIL import Image from rfdetr import RFDETRSmall image = Image.open("path/to/image.jpg") model = RFDETRSmall() detections = model.predict(image, threshold=0.5) len(detections) # 5 ```
👉 more model connectors - inference Running with [Inference](https://github.com/roboflow/inference) requires a [Roboflow API KEY](https://docs.roboflow.com/api-reference/authentication#retrieve-an-api-key). ```python import supervision as sv from PIL import Image from inference import get_model image = Image.open("path/to/image.jpg") model = get_model(model_id="rfdetr-small", api_key="ROBOFLOW_API_KEY") result = model.infer(image)[0] detections = sv.Detections.from_inference(result) len(detections) # 5 ```
### Annotators Supervision offers a wide range of highly customizable [annotators](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/detection/annotators/), allowing you to compose the perfect visualization for your use case. ```python import cv2 import supervision as sv image = cv2.imread("path/to/image.jpg") # Assuming detections are obtained from a model detections = sv.Detections(...) box_annotator = sv.BoxAnnotator() annotated_frame = box_annotator.annotate(scene=image.copy(), detections=detections) ``` https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/assets/26109316/691e219c-0565-4403-9218-ab5644f39bce ### Datasets Supervision provides a set of [utils](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/datasets/core/) that allow you to load, split, merge, and save datasets in one of the supported formats. ```python import supervision as sv from roboflow import Roboflow project = Roboflow().workspace("WORKSPACE_ID").project("PROJECT_ID") dataset = project.version("PROJECT_VERSION").download("coco") ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco( images_directory_path=f"{dataset.location}/train", annotations_path=f"{dataset.location}/train/_annotations.coco.json", ) path, image, annotation = ds[0] # loads image on demand for path, image, annotation in ds: # loads image on demand pass ```
👉 more dataset utils - load ```python dataset = sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., data_yaml_path=..., ) dataset = sv.DetectionDataset.from_pascal_voc( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., ) dataset = sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco( images_directory_path=..., annotations_path=..., ) ``` - split ```python train_dataset, test_dataset = dataset.split(split_ratio=0.7) test_dataset, valid_dataset = test_dataset.split(split_ratio=0.5) len(train_dataset), len(test_dataset), len(valid_dataset) # (700, 150, 150) ``` - merge ```python ds_1 = sv.DetectionDataset(...) len(ds_1) # 100 ds_1.classes # ['dog', 'person'] ds_2 = sv.DetectionDataset(...) len(ds_2) # 200 ds_2.classes # ['cat'] ds_merged = sv.DetectionDataset.merge([ds_1, ds_2]) len(ds_merged) # 300 ds_merged.classes # ['cat', 'dog', 'person'] ``` - save ```python dataset.as_yolo( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., data_yaml_path=..., ) dataset.as_pascal_voc( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., ) dataset.as_coco( images_directory_path=..., annotations_path=..., ) ``` - convert ```python sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., data_yaml_path=..., ).as_pascal_voc( images_directory_path=..., annotations_directory_path=..., ) ```
## 🎬 Tutorials Want to learn how to use Supervision? Explore our [how-to guides](https://supervision.roboflow.com/develop/how_to/detect_and_annotate/), [end-to-end examples](./examples), [cheatsheet](https://roboflow.github.io/cheatsheet-supervision/), and [cookbooks](https://supervision.roboflow.com/develop/cookbooks/)!

👋 Hello

We are your essential toolkit for computer vision. From data loading to real-time zone counting, we provide the building blocks so you can focus on building applications around your models. 🤝

💻 Install

Pip install the supervision package in a Python>=3.10 environment.

pip install supervision

Read more about conda, mamba, and installing from source in our guide.

🔥 Quickstart

Models

Supervision was designed to be model agnostic. Just plug in any classification, detection, or segmentation model. For your convenience, we have created connectors for the most popular libraries like Ultralytics, Transformers, MMDetection, or Inference. Other integrations, like rfdetr, already return sv.Detections directly.

Install the optional dependencies for this example with pip install pillow rfdetr.

import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image
from rfdetr import RFDETRSmall

image = Image.open("path/to/image.jpg")
model = RFDETRSmall()
detections = model.predict(image, threshold=0.5)

len(detections)

releases.name: supervision-0.32.3
releases.body:
# v0.32.3: oriented soft-NMS, stable Pascal VOC ids and crowd-aware metrics

A patch release that adds soft-NMS for rotated boxes and fixes results that came out wrong or raised errors.

- **Oriented soft-NMS** scores rotated boxes by their real overlap, so boxes that only touch keep their scores.
- `KeyPoints.from_inference` takes **`num_keypoints`**, so frames keep the full skeleton when trailing key points were filtered out.
- Pascal VOC train and valid splits with the same classes now get the same class ids.
- Precision, Recall and F1Score stop counting COCO crowd regions as misses and false positives.
- `JSONSink` writes `NaN` as `null`, so strict JSON parsers can read the file.

Drop-in for most users, but a few results shift, so skim the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Oriented soft-NMS measures the overlap of rotated boxes

`sv.Detections.with_soft_nms` decayed oriented-box detections by their axis-aligned envelopes, so two rotated boxes that only touch along an edge still lost score. The new `sv.oriented_box_soft_non_max_suppression` computes the overlap on the four corners of each box, and `with_soft_nms` uses it when `data["xyxyxyxy"]`

releases.name: supervision-0.32.2
releases.body:
# v0.32.2: correct YOLO classes, pose joints and VLM parsing

A patch release that fixes results which used to come out silently wrong.

- **YOLO datasets** with `names` starting above 0 load every label under its real class.
- ViTPose results keep each joint in its own skeleton slot, and a new `num_keypoints` argument fixes the skeleton size.
- Qwen answers that used to parse to nothing now give their detections, and one unreadable Gemini box no longer fails the whole response.
- Browser-recorded WebM videos keep their real speed.
- Objects whose mask drops out for a frame stay put instead of jumping to the image corner.

Drop-in for most users, but a few results shift and a few malformed inputs now raise, so skim the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### YOLO class ids follow `data.yaml`

`data.yaml` may declare `names` as a dict whose keys start above 0 or skip values, such as `{1: cat, 2: dog}`. `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` and `sv.KeyPointsDataset.from_yolo` used the label id as a list index, so labels in such a dataset loaded under the wrong class, or the load failed with an out-of-range `ValueError`. releases.name: supervision-0.32.1
releases.body:
# v0.32.1: BGRA scenes and metric fixes

A patch release: annotators now work on BGRA images, and several metric and dataset results are corrected.

- **Annotators** draw on BGRA scenes with an alpha channel instead of failing with shape errors.
- **`ConfusionMatrix.plot`** with `normalize=True` now divides by true-class rows, so the diagonal is per-class recall.
- **`MeanAverageRecall`** returns `-1` when there is nothing to recall, not a misleading `0.0`.
- **Dataset `split`** keeps the train item that float rounding used to drop.
- Windows users can read and write images in folders with non-ASCII names.
- Edge cases found in review are fixed too: alpha-weighted resizing of translucent BGRA images, rich label text placement, and `np.float16` split ratios.

Upgrading is safe and nothing breaks, but a few metric, split and rendering results shift, so skim the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Annotators and drawing helpers work on BGRA scenes

Scenes shaped `(H, W, 4)`, such as frames with an alpha channel, now work. `sv.MaskAnnotator`, `sv.HaloAnnotator`, `sv.BackgroundOverlayAnnotator`, `sv.ComparisonAnnotator`, `sv.HeatMapAnnotator`, `sv.CropAn

releases.name: supervision-0.32.0
releases.body:
# v0.32.0: Zone counting, dwell time and semantic segmentation

## 📋 Summary

supervision now counts objects entering and leaving a zone, times how long each one stays, and loads semantic segmentation results.

- **`PolygonZone`** counts entries and exits per class and reports dwell time for every tracked object.
- **`Detections.from_semantic_segmentation`** turns a class map into one masked detection per class; Ultralytics and Inference results load too.
- **`KeyPointsDataset`** reads and writes YOLO pose datasets.
- **`box_weighted_box_fusion`** merges overlapping boxes from several models instead of throwing most of them away.
- **`VertexAnnotator`** and its siblings take a color palette and can color each joint by its index.

Most projects can upgrade as is, but the public `validate_*` helpers, `merge_inner_*` and `KeyPoints.confidence` are gone and a few edge cases changed, so check the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Zones that count entries, exits and dwell time

`sv.PolygonZone` now follows each `tracker_id` across frames. It counts objects entering and leaving (`in_count`, `out_count` and the per-class versions are named the same as o

releases.name: supervision-0.31.7
releases.body:
# v0.31.7: pycocotools-matching mAP, stricter key point and CSV inputs, and edge-case fixes for zones and dataset exports

A fixes-only patch: mAP now matches pycocotools more closely, and several zone, key point and export edge cases stop failing.

- **MeanAveragePrecision** uses pycocotools size buckets and the COCO crowd IoU for oriented-box crowd targets.
- **PolygonZone** keeps its full mask when polygon coordinates reach their integer limit.
- Key point selection and **CSVSink** now raise on inputs they used to silently misread.
- **DetectionDataset** exports keep box area for empty COCO masks and, with simplification on, bridge more mask holes.
- The OpenCV-free `contourArea` and `convertScaleAbs` fallbacks agree with OpenCV in more cases.

Drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you compare mAP values, pass extra CSV fields or select key points with boolean masks.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### `MeanAveragePrecision` matches `pycocotools` more closely

aiSummary.oneLiner: A reusable computer vision utility library for writing robust detection and tracking pipelines.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Supervision is an open-source Python library designed to simplify the development of computer vision applications. It acts as a universal bridge between various object detection models (like YOLOv8, Ultralytics, and HuggingFace models) and practical application logic. Instead of writing boilerplate code for parsing complex model outputs, drawing bounding boxes, tracking object trajectories across frames, or filtering detections by specific zones, developers can use Supervision's high-level API. This dramatically accelerates the deployment of AI models into production environments by handling the tedious post-processing steps of computer vision workflows.
keyFeatures: Model Agnostic API: Provides a unified interface to process outputs from almost any object detection or segmentation model.
Advanced Annotators: Includes a wide array of highly customizable drawing tools for bounding boxes, polygons, and labels.
Object Tracking Integration: Seamlessly integrates robust multi-object tracking algorithms to follow entities across video frames.
Zone Filtering: Allows developers to define specific polygonal zones to filter detections or trigger events based on spatial location.
Dataset Management: Offers utilities for converting, filtering, and merging computer vision datasets in various formats.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Computer vision engineers, machine learning researchers, and developers building AI-powered video analytics applications. It is the go-to tool for rapidly translating raw model outputs into actionable data and visualizations.
